clips.send: Credit. Buy now, pay later — plus interest. APR equals the yearly interest rate on a loan or card balance. Pay the full statement balance each month and a card usually charges no interest. Paying late hurts your credit score, which lenders use to decide future loans and rates.

clips.send: Scams and fraud. Tricks that try to get your money or your passwords. Scammers pretend to be someone you trust, invent a problem or prize, rush you, and demand an odd payment method. Real companies never ask you to pay with gift cards or to share a login code. Report US scams at ReportFraud.ftc.gov; in China, the National Anti-Fraud Center (国家反诈中心) runs an app and the 96110 warning line.

clips.send: Saving. Setting money aside for goals, emergencies and the future. Reasons to save: a goal (bike, college), emergencies, and the future. An emergency fund turns a surprise bill into a small problem instead of a debt. US bank deposits are insured by the FDIC up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category.

clips.send: Budget. A plan for spending and saving before the money is gone. List income, then needs, savings and wants. 50/30/20 is a common rule of thumb: 50 percent needs, 30 percent wants, 20 percent savings — not a law. “Pay yourself first”: move savings out as soon as money arrives.

clips.send: Income. Money coming in — where every money plan starts. Income from work is limited: there are only so many hours to babysit, mow or work a shift. Teens earn from allowances, gifts (like red-envelope money, 压岁钱) and small jobs. On a paycheck, taxes come out first: gross pay is before taxes, net pay is what you keep.

clips.send: Compound interest. Interest that earns interest — growth that speeds up over time. Simple interest is paid only on what you put in; compound interest is also paid on earlier interest. Rule of 72: years to double about 72 divided by interest rate (percent). Time matters most: starting 10 years earlier can beat saving more later.

clips.send: 收入。进来的钱——一切理财计划的起点。 工作收入是有限的：能用来照看小孩、割草或打工的时间就那么多。 青少年的钱来自零花钱、礼金（比如压岁钱）和小零工。 工资单上先扣税：税前是“应发工资”，到手的才是“实发工资”。

clips.send: 诈骗与欺诈。想骗走你的钱或密码的伎俩。 骗子冒充你信任的人，编造问题或奖品，催你快点，并要求奇怪的付款方式。 正规公司从不让你用礼品卡付款，也不会索要登录验证码。 在美国可到 ReportFraud.ftc.gov 举报；在中国，国家反诈中心有 App 和 96110 预警电话。

clips.send: 预算。在钱花掉之前做好的支出和储蓄计划。 先列收入，再列需要、储蓄和想要。 50/30/20 是一个常见的经验法则：需要 百分之50，想要 百分之30，储蓄 百分之20——不是硬性规定。 “先付给自己”：钱一到手，先把储蓄的那份拿出来。

clips.send: 储蓄。为目标、应急和未来把钱留出来。 储蓄的理由：实现目标（自行车、上大学）、应对意外、为了将来。 有了应急基金，一笔意外账单只是小麻烦，而不会变成欠债。 在美国，银行存款由联邦存款保险公司，F D I C，保险，每位存款人在每家银行、每种账户类型最高 25 万美元。

clips.send: 复利。利息再生利息——随时间越滚越快的增长。 单利只按本金计息；复利连以前的利息也一起计息。 72 法则：翻倍所需年数 约等于 72 除以 年利率（百分比）。 时间最重要：早 10 年开始，往往比以后多存更有用。

clips.send: 信用与信贷。先买后付——外加利息。 APR 等于 贷款或信用卡欠款的年利率。 每月全额还清账单，信用卡通常不收利息。 逾期还款会拉低信用评分，而银行会根据信用评分决定以后贷不贷款、利率多高。
